facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The issuer's financial base is the filed statements of PBF Holding Company LLC. They show a sharp turn from a trough to a strong position within three quarters. FY2025 was a loss year: a net loss of 481.3, income from operations of -292.6 even after an 832.5 gain on insurance recoveries, and company-defined Adjusted EBITDA of only 29.5 (10K page:123 "Adjusted EBITDA $ 29.5 $ (79.9) $ 2,408.0"). In the first nine months of 2026 net income was 3,269.6 and Adjusted EBITDA was 3,284.3 (Q3-10Q page:59 "Adjusted EBITDA $ 2,139.3 $ 91.5 $ 3,284.3 $ (191.4)"). Management attributes the increase to crack spreads and crude differentials affected by geopolitical conflict and to higher throughput after the Martinez restart (Q3-10Q page:43 "a significant increase in refining margins"); this is management language and is not adopted as a forecast. Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 supply 3,278.6 of the 3,505.2 LTM Adjusted EBITDA, so the trailing figure is exposed to whether those margins persist. Debt was reorganised during 2026: the 2028 6.00% and 2030 7.875% notes were redeemed, 500.0 of 2034 7.25% notes and 550.0 of 2032 exchangeable notes were issued, and the revolver was amended and extended; at 30 September 2026 principal debt was 1,850.0 against cash of 2,510.6, and on 26 October 2026, after the period, the 800.0 of 2030 9.875% notes were redeemed using cash on hand. Leverage on company Adjusted EBITDA is therefore distorted at both ends of the series: not meaningful at FY2024 and FY2025 because EBITDA is negative or near zero, and very low at LTM Q3 2026. Interest cover uses cash interest paid net of capitalised interest and so overstates cover relative to total interest. Debt is only part of the claim stack: lease, pension, purchase, environmental, emissions and legal claims sit outside it and are set out below. Liquidity is printed as rounded narrative amounts whose build cannot be reproduced from the pack. Perimeter discipline matters: the parent's releases print different cash, debt and operating income, and none of them is used for an issuer figure. This view is a financial extraction and a structured set of limitations; it is not a credit rating, a recommendation or a forecast.

facts.label: Liquidity and covenants
facts.text: Covenants. The only maintenance test is springing (10K page:181 "PBF Holding will not permit the Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio, as defined in the Revolving Credit Agreement and determined as of the last day of the most recently completed quarter, to be less than 1 to 1") and applies only when excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base and commitments and 100.0. The issuer reports compliance (Q3-10Q page:24 "the Company is in compliance with all covenants, including financial covenants, in all its debt agreements") but prints no ratio and no headroom. The notes carry incurrence covenants limiting debt, equity issuances, payments and investments, which fall away on a covenant termination event such as an investment grade rating (Q3-10Q page:23). Definition difference: the test uses "Excess Availability" and a fixed charge coverage ratio defined in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, whereas this handoff uses company-defined Adjusted EBITDA and printed borrowing availability; they are different measures.

facts.label: Consistency with CP-0 and conflicts
facts.text: 1. Covenant wording. CP-0 stated that the Q3 10-Q does not restate the covenant test and listed only rates, fees, defaults and indemnification as consistent with the prior agreement. The Q3 sentence in fact says (Q3-10Q page:24 "representations, warranties and covenants by PBF Holding and the other borrowers, as well as customary events of default and indemnification obligations that are consistent with those in the Prior Credit Agreement"). It does not print the fixed charge test again, but it does say the covenants are consistent with the prior agreement. This corrects the CP-0 phrasing; the CP-0 handoff itself is not edited. 2. Borrowing base. CP-0 recorded that no borrowing base figure was supplied for liquidity. The 10-K does print a facility table with borrowing base availability of 2,296.6 at 2025-12-31 (10K page:129). The 10-Qs do not. Liquidity for 2026 dates therefore still rests on rounded narrative amounts. 3. Issuer versus parent debt, cash and operating income (CP-0 conflicts 1 to 3) remain unreconciled and are not used. 4. Distributions to members in 9M 2026: the equity statement prints 156.4 (Q3-10Q page:9) and the cash flow statement prints 156.3 (Q3-10Q page:10); a rounding-level difference that does not affect any figure here. 5. Liquidity build. At 2025-12-31 the narrative availability of more than 1.8 billion plus cash of 503.0 is consistent with the table's 2,296.6, which suggests cash is inside the table figure; at 2026-09-30 the narrative total of 5.6 billion exceeds the 4,000.0 commitment less 157.2 of letters of credit, so the build cannot be reproduced. This is recorded as a limitation, not resolved.

rows.label: The issuer moved from a trough in FY2025 to strong earnings and net cash by 30 September 2026, but that rests on two strong refining quarters and on company-defined EBITDA. A further redemption followed quarter end.
Adjusted EBITDA was 29.5 in FY2025 and 3,505.2 for the twelve months to Q3 2026, almost all earned in Q2 and Q3 2026.
Principal debt was 1,850.0 against cash of 2,510.6 at 30 September 2026, a net cash position of 660.6.
The 2026 refinancing replaced 2028 and 2030 notes with 2032 exchangeable and 2034 notes and extended the revolver to 2031.
Cash interest paid was 162.3 for the twelve months to Q3 2026, and the figure is net of capitalised interest.
Obligations outside debt include leases, pension deficits, purchase commitments, environmental and emissions liabilities and unquantified Martinez investigations.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The issuer, PBF Holding Company LLC, is the borrowing and operating holding company for six U.S. refineries with about 1,000,000 barrels per day of capacity, reported as one segment, and it is wholly owned by PBF Energy Company LLC under the listed parent PBF Energy Inc. Its revenue is the sale of unbranded fuels and other refined products at prevailing market prices, almost 89% of it gasoline and distillates, to a diverse base with one customer, Shell, at about 13% of revenue. Because crude and product prices both float, the business has little pricing control: results depend on industry crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput, refinery reliability and the cost of renewable fuel credits. That mechanism explains the swing from a loss year in FY2025, when the Martinez refinery was shut and then restarting, to very large earnings in 2026, when management says geopolitical conflict widened margins and the Martinez refinery returned to full operations in May 2026. The creditor reading is that the operating model is cyclical and event-exposed, with the business risk concentrated in refinery uptime, margin volatility, environmental and emissions obligations and legal investigations, rather than in customer or contract concentration. The transaction picture in 2026 is a refinancing and simplification: the 6.00% notes due 2028 and the 7.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed, 500.0 of 7.25% notes due 2034 and 550.0 of zero-coupon exchangeable notes due 2032 were issued, the asset-based revolver was amended to a 4,000.0 commitment through 2031-09-30, and after the quarter the 9.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed on 2026-10-26 with cash on hand. The new exchangeable notes are exchangeable into shares of the parent, which links the issuer's liabilities and reported earnings to the parent's share price. Ownership is a listed-parent structure with no financial sponsor named in the pack, and documented behaviour toward creditors is mixed: parent cash contributions and full-par or premium note redemptions are supportive, while distributions to the parent chain to fund its dividends, past asset distributions to affiliates and the parent-level secured note on the hydrogen plants are items a creditor should track. This is a fact pack, not a rating or a recommendation.

facts.text: 2032 0.00% exchangeable senior notes. Type: new senior unsecured exchangeable notes with an embedded exchange option and capped call. Parties: PBF Holding and PBF Finance as issuers, PBF Energy Inc. as a party to the indenture and registration rights agreement, U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee. Status: completed 2026-09-17. Amount: 550.0; net proceeds about 533.2, of which 27.7 paid for the capped call and the rest, with cash, redeemed the 2030 7.875% notes (Q3-10Q page:18 "The Issuers used $27.7 million of the net proceeds to pay the cost of the capped call transactions"). Terms: no regular interest and no principal accretion (Q3-10Q page:18 "The 2032 Exchangeable Notes do not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the 2032 Exchangeable Notes will not accrete."), maturity 2032-01-15, initial exchange rate of 10.3306 PBF Energy Class A shares per 1,000 of principal (Q3-10Q page:18 "initial exchange rate is 10.3306 shares of PBF Energy Class A common stock, per $1,000 principal amount"), exchange price about $96.80, capped call cap price about $123.20 (Q3-10Q page:21 "initial cap price of approximately $123.20 per share"), settlement in cash up to principal with the excess in cash or PBF Energy shares at the issuers' election (Q3-10Q page:18 "will be settled in cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being exchanged"). Mechanics: the exchange feature is a bifurcated derivative liability that the issuer marks to fair value, at 197.6 at 2026-09-30 with a 29.9 unrealized loss in Q3 2026, using a PBF Energy share price input of $76.96 (Q3-10Q page:31 "Share price $ 76.96"); the debt host carries a large discount with an effective rate of about 7.0%. Creditor implication: zero cash coupon lowers cash interest, but the issuer carries the principal in cash settlement, the derivative creates earnings volatility linked to the parent's share price, and the instrument depends on parent equity; Analyst Interpretation. A registration rights agreement requires PBF Energy to file a shelf by 2026-12-31 with special interest of 0.25% rising to 0.50% if the issuers fail to comply (Q3-10Q page:20 "on or prior to December 31, 2026").

facts.text: Hydrogen plants asset purchase. Type: purchase of two hydrogen plants at the Torrance refinery previously under operating leases. Parties: PBF LLC and Air Products; contributed to the issuer. Status: closed 2026-09-09. facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability and margin risk. Evidence: revenues are priced at spot market (Q3-10Q page:28 "These revenues are largely based on the current spot (market) prices of the products sold") and the Q3 2026 margin rise is attributed by management to crack spreads and differentials (Q3-10Q page:45 "Average industry margins were notably more favorable"). Risk mechanic: no price floor and no contractual margin, so cash flow tracks external spreads and refinery uptime. Credit implication: debt service capacity is high when spreads are wide and thin when they narrow, as FY2025 showed with Adjusted EBITDA of 29.5; the trailing LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,505.2 rests on two quarters. Counter-evidence logged: management says refining fundamentals remained exceptionally strong (Q3-PR page:1 "refining fundamentals remained exceptionally strong"), Management Language not adopted as a forecast. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 2. Refinancing and liquidity. Evidence: the 2026 notes sequence, the revolver extension to 2031-09-30 and cash of 2,510.6 at 2026-09-30 with 800.0 redeemed afterwards. Risk mechanic: removal of 2028 and 2030 maturities and the zero-coupon exchangeable lowers refinancing and interest burden; the secured revolver ranks ahead of unsecured notes in collateral. Credit implication: refinancing risk is low in the near term for this perimeter; effective subordination of the unsecured notes to the revolver and to the parent-linked exchange feature should be monitored. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 3. Concentration. Evidence: Shell at about 13% of revenue, six refineries across four regions. Risk mechanic: customer concentration is modest; asset concentration is in the Martinez and Torrance West Coast refineries and regulatory exposure in California. Credit implication: event risk at one refinery (as the Martinez fire showed) matters more than customer loss. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 4. Sponsor alignment and leakage. Evidence: distributions to the parent chain, asset distributions to PBFX and SBR, parent dividend funding language, hydrogen contribution. Risk mechanic: cash can move up to fund parent dividends when liquidity is strong; restricted payment covenants are not supplied. Credit implication: Neutral or Mixed; monitor distributions against liquidity and the hydrogen note security. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: unquantified Martinez investigations, the Chalmette fire, the hydrogen note, labour agreements and the missing documents. Credit implication: open items could add cash costs or lien constraints; they are information gaps, not adverse conclusions.

rows.label: The issuer is a six-refinery, one-segment operating subsidiary of a listed parent, now with simplified debt and minimal near-term maturities. Earnings are market-driven, and several parent-linked and event items remain open.
The issuer sells commodity fuels at market prices from six refineries, so cash flow follows crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput and compliance costs.
In 2026 the issuer replaced 2028 and 2030 notes with 2034 notes and exchangeable notes and extended the revolver to 2031.
The parent chain receives distributions and has contributed assets and cash; the hydrogen plants came in from the parent under terms the issuer does not fully describe.
The Martinez fire investigations are unquantified and a May 2026 Chalmette fire is named without any amount.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: PBF Holding Company LLC has a sound credit profile at 30 September 2026 that has not yet been tested through a normal-margin year. Its strongest support is liquidity and leverage: USD 2,510.6 million of cash against USD 1,850.0 million of debt principal, net cash of USD 660.6 million, and a USD 4,000.0 million revolver running to 30 September 2031. Its weakest point is earnings durability: Adjusted EBITDA was USD 29.5 million in FY2025 and USD 3,505.2 million over the twelve months to Q3 2026, with USD 3,278.6 million earned in two quarters. What decides the outcome is whether refining margins hold while cash can leave for the parent and the open fire, legal and hydrogen plants items are resolved.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The issuer has low reported leverage and net cash: 0.5x total debt and -0.2x net debt to twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, and cash interest paid of USD 162.3 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,505.2 million, or 21.6x cover on a measure that excludes capitalised interest [CP-1 interest cover]. Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading. The issuer has liquidity depth, with USD 2,510.6 million of cash and about USD 3,100.0 million of rounded borrowing availability, and no revolver drawing at the quarter end [CP-1 liquidity]. Its maturity profile has no drawn debt maturing before 2032 after the October redemption [CP-1 debt maturities]. Its asset base is diversified across six refineries in four regions with one customer at about 13% of revenue, so customer loss is a smaller risk than a single refinery event [CP-1A operating model]. The parent supported the issuer with net contributions of USD 199.6 million in the FY2025 downturn and contributed the hydrogen plants in Q3 2026 [CP-1A ownership and behaviour].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. The issuer's earnings depend on external margins and uptime: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 29.5 million in FY2025 against USD 3,505.2 million over the latest twelve months, with USD 3,278.6 million from two quarters. Analyst Interpretation resting on the CP-1 figures. The issuer faces event risk at single sites: the Martinez fire investigations and the 8 May 2026 Chalmette fire have no quantified impact [CP-1A transaction summary]. Cash can leave to the parent chain and the exchangeable notes link the issuer to the parent's share price, with a fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million [CP-1A behaviour table; CP-1 debt instruments]. Large claims sit outside debt, notably leases, purchase commitments, emissions credits and environmental liabilities [CP-1 claims outside debt]. The revolver is secured and ranks ahead of the unsecured notes to the extent of its collateral; the unsecured notes are also structurally behind non-guarantor subsidiaries, a structural mechanic and not a recovery conclusion [CP-1 debt instruments]. Regulatory compliance cost is large and volatile: renewable fuel compliance cost was USD 522.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 169.0 million a year earlier [CP-1A operating model].

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: PBF Holding Co LLC (issuer id pbf-holding-co-llc). The filings name the registrant "PBF Holding Company LLC" and its co-registrant "PBF Finance Corporation". The filings are the evidence for the identity; the context file only supplies the short name.

As-of date and evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD. Current period q3-2026, prior period fy-2025 (context). All filed amounts are in USD millions unless a source says otherwise.

Task of this module: source readiness only. It judges whether the pinned source set can support the four requested downstream modules (CP-1 financial extraction, CP-1A business and transaction context, CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis, CP-5 evidence trace and research integrity) and what remains blocked. It gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it normalises, reconciles and calculates no financial figure. Citations below use the form (label page:N "exact substring"), where the label is defined in the Sources table and N is the source chunk number, not the printed page.

Context inputs (not issuer evidence): the context file leaves deal terms, quotes, ratings, valuation inputs, peers, assumptions and research questions empty, names no borrower, parent or guarantors, and states no legal documents attached. Those blanks are not treated as zero.

### Conflicts and differences to carry forward

1. Debt definition and perimeter at 2026-09-30. The issuer's balance sheet prints long-term debt of 1,613.0 (Q3-10Q page:7 "Long-term debt 1,613.0 2,148.3") and its debt table sums to 1,850.0 principal before deferred financing costs of 63.0 and discount of 174.0 (Q3-10Q page:17 "1,850.0 2,201.6"; "Unamortized discount (174.0) (12.3)"). Downstream effect: any leverage, net debt or capitalisation figure must say which perimeter and definition it uses; the two are not reconciled here.
2. Cash at 2026-09-30: issuer 2,510.6 (Q3-10Q page:7) against parent 2,544.3 (Q3-PR page:8). Same effect as above.

3. Operating income for the third quarter of 2026: issuer 1,988.3 (Q3-10Q page:8), parent 2,100.9 (Q3-PR page:1) and summarized guarantor group 2,632.8 (Q3-10Q page:70). The Q3 release states (Q3-PR page:1 "net debt reduction of 150% as compared to the second quarter of 2026") and (Q3-PR page:2 "approximately $2.1 billion of total debt, and $426 million of net cash"). 5. Liquidity wording. The issuer states (Q3-10Q page:66 "approximately $3.1 billion of borrowing availability under our Revolving Credit Facility, which includes our cash on hand") and an operational liquidity "over $5.6 billion" made up of cash and availability. The phrase "which includes our cash on hand" leaves it unclear whether availability and cash overlap. The same wording appears at every period (10K page:130, Q1-10Q page:42, Q2-10Q page:54). No borrowing base certificate is supplied to settle it. Downstream effect: liquidity must be quoted as printed, with the ambiguity noted, and not rebuilt.

6. Ratings. The only rating statement is in the 10-K, dated before the 2026 refinancing: (10K page:77 "are rated B1 by Moody’s, BB by S&P, and BB by Fitch"). It lists the 2028 6.00%, 2030 7.875% and 2030 9.875% notes; the first two were redeemed in 2026 (Q3-10Q page:17 shows both at nil), so the statement is stale for the current notes. No rating of the 2034 7.25% notes or the 2032 exchangeable notes is in the pack.
### Subsequent events and period discipline

Events after 2026-09-30 and before the cutoff must stay out of 30 September balances. The Q3 10-Q reports (Q3-10Q page:33 "On October 26, 2026, PBF Holding redeemed all $800.0 million in aggregate principal amount of its outstanding 2030 9.875% Senior Notes") at (Q3-10Q page:33 "The aggregate redemption price of the 2030 9.875% Senior Notes redeemed was approximately $853.4 million"), funded from cash on hand; the 800.0 is still in the 30 September debt table (Q3-10Q page:17). Within the third quarter, the revolver was amended and restated on 2026-09-30 (Q3-10Q page:24 "increased the maximum commitment from $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion"). Nothing dated after 2026-11-05 is used.

- Financial reports: statements, notes, period labels, debt, liquidity and covenants are present in the 10-K and 10-Qs. The segment position is a single reportable segment (Q3-10Q page:34 "Our six oil refineries are aggregated into one reportable segment"), so there is no segment table to extract. - Covenant evidence: the only financial covenant description is in the 10-K, a springing test (10K page:181 "to be less than 1 to 1"; full text "Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio, as defined in the Revolving Credit Agreement") that applies only below a minimum excess availability. The 10-Qs give compliance statements (Q3-10Q page:24 "the Company is in compliance with all covenants, including financial covenants, in all its debt agreements") but no ratio level or headroom. The Q3 10-Q does not restate the test after the 2026-09-30 amendment and says only that the interest rate, letter of credit fees, events of default and indemnification obligations are generally consistent with the prior agreement (Q3-10Q page:24 "customary events of default and indemnification obligations that are consistent with those in the Prior Credit Agreement").

- Legal and financing sources: no executed indenture, credit agreement, capped call confirmation or registration rights agreement is in the pack; the Q3 10-Q lists them as incorporated by reference (Q3-10Q page:83 "Amended and Restated Senior Secured Revolving Credit Agreement, dated September 30, 2026 (incorporated by reference"). ### Financial base view

The issuer's financial base is the filed statements of PBF Holding Company LLC. They show a sharp turn from a trough to a strong position within three quarters. FY2025 was a loss year: a net loss of 481.3, income from operations of -292.6 even after an 832.5 gain on insurance recoveries, and company-defined Adjusted EBITDA of only 29.5 (10K page:123 "Adjusted EBITDA $ 29.5 $ (79.9) $ 2,408.0"). In the first nine months of 2026 net income was 3,269.6 and Adjusted EBITDA was 3,284.3 (Q3-10Q page:59 "Adjusted EBITDA $ 2,139.3 $ 91.5 $ 3,284.3 $ (191.4)"). Management attributes the increase to crack spreads and crude differentials affected by geopolitical conflict and to higher throughput after the Martinez restart (Q3-10Q page:43 "a significant increase in refining margins"); this is management language and is not adopted as a forecast. Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 supply 3,278.6 of the 3,505.2 LTM Adjusted EBITDA, so the trailing figure is exposed to whether those margins persist. Debt was reorganised during 2026: the 2028 6.00% and 2030 7.875% notes were redeemed, 500.0 of 2034 7.25% notes and 550.0 of 2032 exchangeable notes were issued, and the revolver was amended and extended; at 30 September 2026 principal debt was 1,850.0 against cash of 2,510.6, and on 26 October 2026, after the period, the 800.0 of 2030 9.875% notes were redeemed using cash on hand. Leverage on company Adjusted EBITDA is therefore distorted at both ends of the series: not meaningful at FY2024 and FY2025 because EBITDA is negative or near zero, and very low at LTM Q3 2026. Interest cover uses cash interest paid net of capitalised interest and so overstates cover relative to total interest. Debt is only part of the claim stack: lease, pension, purchase, environmental, emissions and legal claims sit outside it and are set out below. Liquidity is printed as rounded narrative amounts whose build cannot be reproduced from the pack. Perimeter discipline matters: the parent's releases print different cash, debt and operating income, and none of them is used for an issuer figure. This view is a financial extraction and a structured set of limitations; it is not a credit rating, a recommendation or a forecast.

### Liquidity and covenants

Liquidity. The issuer prints operational liquidity as cash plus revolver borrowing availability (Q3-10Q page:66 "our operational liquidity was over $5.6 billion"), made up of cash of about 2.5 billion and availability of about 3.1 billion, with letters of credit of about 157.2 (Q3-10Q page:66 "outstanding letters of credit totaled approximately $157.2 million"). These are rounded narrative figures; the build is shown in Calculations. Facility-by-facility, only one revolver is reported. The 10-K prints a facility table (10K page:129 "Revolving Credit Facility (a) $ 3,500.0 $ 100.0 $ 167.3 $ 2,296.6 August 2028") whose borrowing base includes 100% of cash in controlled deposit accounts; no later table is printed. The facility that expired in August 2028 was replaced by the amended revolver expiring 2031-09-30, so no facility expires within twelve months of the cutoff.

Covenants. The only maintenance test is springing (10K page:181 "PBF Holding will not permit the Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio, as defined in the Revolving Credit Agreement and determined as of the last day of the most recently completed quarter, to be less than 1 to 1") and applies only when excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base and commitments and 100.0. The issuer reports compliance (Q3-10Q page:24 "the Company is in compliance with all covenants, including financial covenants, in all its debt agreements") but prints no ratio and no headroom. The notes carry incurrence covenants limiting debt, equity issuances, payments and investments, which fall away on a covenant termination event such as an investment grade rating (Q3-10Q page:23). Definition difference: the test uses "Excess Availability" and a fixed charge coverage ratio defined in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, whereas this handoff uses company-defined Adjusted EBITDA and printed borrowing availability; they are different measures.

### Illustrative effects of the 2026-10-26 redemption (subsequent event, not a reported balance)
| Item | Formula with inputs | Result |
| Cash after the redemption price, before accrued interest and other flows | 2,510.6 - 853.4 | 1,657.2 |

### Liquidity cross-checks
| Date | Commitment less drawn less letters of credit | Printed availability | Cash plus printed availability | Printed total |

The commitment-based figure is an upper bound, not an availability: printed availability is lower than commitment less usage on every date, consistent with a borrowing base limit. The covenant trigger cross-check: the largest possible testing amount is 10% of 4,000.0 = 400.0 (the lesser of borrowing base and commitments cannot exceed the commitment), above the 100.0 floor; printed availability of about 3,100.0 is about 2,700.0 above that, so the springing test appears not to be in effect at 2026-09-30. This is an Analyst Interpretation resting on the printed approximate availability and on a definition of Excess Availability that is not supplied.
### Derived fact checks

- Leases: operating 163.0 + 60.1 + 399.0 + 90.2 = 712.3 (Q3-10Q page:7); financing 16.1 + 12.8 = 28.9. At 2025-12-31 operating 184.2 + 141.2 + 541.4 + 114.7 = 981.5; with financing 25.8 + 12.2 = 38.0 the total is 1,019.5, matching the printed total lease liabilities.

- Adjusted EBITDA definition check, Q3 2026: EBITDA 2,092.5 + stock compensation 7.8 + RBI costs 11.0 + loss on extinguishment 28.0 = 2,139.3, equal to the printed figure. The 29.9 unrealized loss on the exchange feature is not added back, so Adjusted EBITDA is stated after that loss.

## Next module

Proceed to CP-1A. It should take the 2026 refinancing sequence, the revolver amendment, the hydrogen plants purchase, the Martinez fire and insurance history, the ownership chain and the subsequent events from the Findings above, and carry H1, H6, H7 and H10. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD, amounts in USD millions unless stated. Current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025.

Task of this module: the business and transaction fact pack a committee reads first, from the creditor's view. It answers which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most, and carries them through evidence, risk mechanic and credit implication. Perimeter: PBF Holding Company LLC and its consolidated subsidiaries as filed; the parent PBF Energy Inc. is named only as owner and as issuer of the earnings releases. Facts are tagged Documentary Fact (the cited source states it), Management Language (management's characterisation, quoted and not adopted), Analyst Interpretation (my reading of cited evidence) or Insufficient Information (evidence missing, with the missing datapoint). Citations use the form (label page:N "exact substring"), where N is the source chunk number, not the printed page. Events after 2026-09-30 are labelled Subsequent events and are not folded into period facts. No individual is assessed; behaviour is assessed at issuer level only. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The issuer is a six-refinery, one-segment operating subsidiary of a listed parent, now with simplified debt and minimal near-term maturities. Earnings are market-driven, and several parent-linked and event items remain open. | Medium | The executed financing documents, the hydrogen plants consideration terms and the Martinez and Chalmette outcomes are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The issuer sells commodity fuels at market prices from six refineries, so cash flow follows crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput and compliance costs. | Earnings and cash flow can swing quickly with margins, and this is the main driver of credit risk. | High |

| In 2026 the issuer replaced 2028 and 2030 notes with 2034 notes and exchangeable notes and extended the revolver to 2031. | Maturities moved out and coupon cost fell, but the exchangeable notes tie the issuer to its parent's share price. | High |

| The parent chain receives distributions and has contributed assets and cash; the hydrogen plants came in from the parent under terms the issuer does not fully describe. | Cash can leave the issuer to fund parent dividends, and a parent secured note may touch issuer assets; the pack cannot confirm. | Medium |
| The Martinez fire investigations are unquantified and a May 2026 Chalmette fire is named without any amount. | Possible penalties and outages are open items with no sized impact. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

The issuer, PBF Holding Company LLC, is the borrowing and operating holding company for six U.S. refineries with about 1,000,000 barrels per day of capacity, reported as one segment, and it is wholly owned by PBF Energy Company LLC under the listed parent PBF Energy Inc. Its revenue is the sale of unbranded fuels and other refined products at prevailing market prices, almost 89% of it gasoline and distillates, to a diverse base with one customer, Shell, at about 13% of revenue. Because crude and product prices both float, the business has little pricing control: results depend on industry crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput, refinery reliability and the cost of renewable fuel credits. That mechanism explains the swing from a loss year in FY2025, when the Martinez refinery was shut and then restarting, to very large earnings in 2026, when management says geopolitical conflict widened margins and the Martinez refinery returned to full operations in May 2026. The creditor reading is that the operating model is cyclical and event-exposed, with the business risk concentrated in refinery uptime, margin volatility, environmental and emissions obligations and legal investigations, rather than in customer or contract concentration. The transaction picture in 2026 is a refinancing and simplification: the 6.00% notes due 2028 and the 7.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed, 500.0 of 7.25% notes due 2034 and 550.0 of zero-coupon exchangeable notes due 2032 were issued, the asset-based revolver was amended to a 4,000.0 commitment through 2031-09-30, and after the quarter the 9.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed on 2026-10-26 with cash on hand. The new exchangeable notes are exchangeable into shares of the parent, which links the issuer's liabilities and reported earnings to the parent's share price. Ownership is a listed-parent structure with no financial sponsor named in the pack, and documented behaviour toward creditors is mixed: parent cash contributions and full-par or premium note redemptions are supportive, while distributions to the parent chain to fund its dividends, past asset distributions to affiliates and the parent-level secured note on the hydrogen plants are items a creditor should track. This is a fact pack, not a rating or a recommendation.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Evidence | Credit relevance (mechanic and implication) |

| Revenue streams | Revenue is dominated by gasoline and distillates, with asphalt, feedstocks, chemicals and lubricants smaller; gasoline and distillates were 28,159.0 of 31,703.8 in 9M 2026 and 88.1% of FY2025 revenue | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:28 "Gasoline and distillates $ 28,159.0 $ 19,424.6"); (10K page:27 "gasoline and distillates accounted for 88.1%, 86.6% and 88.8% of our revenues") | Single-product-family exposure means crack spread moves reach nearly all revenue; margin risk, not mix, drives cash flow. |

| Pricing | Revenue is largely based on spot market prices on delivery; some contracts have fixed, tiered or minimum-volume features | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:28 "These revenues are largely based on the current spot (market) prices of the products sold") | No contractual price protection; revenue and margin move with commodity prices, which raises volatility of debt service capacity. |

| Volume drivers | Six refineries, combined capacity of approximately 1,000,000 bpd, weighted average complexity 12.8; Q3 2026 throughput by region 293,800, 156,400, 180,500 and 293,100 bpd, higher mainly on the Martinez restart, partly offset by September turnarounds | Documentary Fact | (10K page:11 "We own and operate six domestic oil refineries and related assets"); (Q3-10Q page:44 "the total throughput rates at our East Coast, Mid-Continent, Gulf Coast, and West Coast refineries averaged approximately 293,800 bpd, 156,400 bpd, 180,500 bpd, and 293,100 bpd, respectively") | Uptime and turnaround timing drive volumes; an unplanned outage hits cash flow directly. |

| Margin drivers | Management attributes the Q3 2026 margin increase to favourable crack spreads and crude differentials affected by geopolitical conflict, partly offset by higher compliance and freight costs | Management Language | (Q3-10Q page:45 "Average industry margins were notably more favorable during the three months ended September 30, 2026 in comparison to the same period in 2025, primarily due to geopolitical conflicts negatively impacting supply with demand remaining relatively resilient") | Margins depend on external conditions the filing itself calls uncertain; persistence cannot be assumed. |

| Cost structure | Refining operating expense per barrel of throughput was $7.80 in Q3 2026 against $7.35 in Q3 2025; natural gas is the main variable cost, and a $1.00 per MMBTU change moves cost by $70.0 million to $100.0 million a year; RFS compliance costs were 522.8 in Q3 2026 against 169.0 | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:42 "Refining operating expense, per barrel of throughput $ 7.80 $ 7.35 $ 8.15 $ 8.56"); (Q3-10Q page:72 "a $1.00 per MMBTU change in natural gas prices would increase or decrease our natural gas costs by approximately $70.0 million to $100.0 million"); (Q3-10Q page:45 "Total RFS compliance costs were $522.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $169.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025") | Energy and credit-compliance costs are large, volatile and partly regulatory; they take margin before debt service. |

| Capital spending | 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $825.0 million to $875.0 million excluding the Martinez rebuild; Chalmette and Toledo fourth-quarter turnarounds moved to 2027 | Management Language | (Q3-10Q page:67 "revised our 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $825.0 million to $875.0 million for the year, excluding capital related to the Martinez refinery rebuild") | Maintenance and turnaround spend is recurring and lumpy; deferred turnarounds shift cash outflow into 2027. |

| Working capital | Inventory is valued on last-in, first-out; at 2026-09-30 replacement cost exceeded carrying value by approximately $1.6 billion, and a 313.0 lower-of-cost-or-market reserve was reversed in 2026 | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:16 "the replacement cost of inventories exceeded their carrying value under the last-in, first-out") | Rising prices tie up cash in receivables and inventory; falling prices could trigger inventory write-downs and release working capital. |

| Customers | One customer, Shell, accounted for approximately 13% of revenue in FY2025 and FY2024; Sunoco buys about one-third of Toledo gasoline and distillates under an agreement expiring June 2027; West Coast offtake with Shell Oil Products runs up to 15 years | Documentary Fact | (10K page:28 "approximately 13% and 13%, respectively"); (10K page:21 "Sunoco purchases gasoline and distillate products representing approximately one-third of the Toledo refinery"); (10K page:24 "offtake agreements for our West Coast system with Shell Oil Products for clean products with varying terms up to 15 years") | Low customer concentration limits single-customer loss risk; offtake renewals are a monitoring point. |

| Supply | The company has no crude reserves and sources crude mainly through short-term and spot agreements | Documentary Fact | (10K page:29 "We have no crude oil reserves and are not engaged in the exploration or production of crude oil"); (10K page:18 "primarily through short-term, spot market, and term agreements") | Supply security depends on markets and logistics; disruptions affect throughput. |

| Related-party flows | Affiliate agreements with PBFX and SBR: total expenses under PBFX affiliate agreements 88.8 in Q3 2026; purchases from SBR 378.2 in Q3 2026 against 132.2 | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:24 "Total expenses under affiliate agreements (88.8) (88.0) (270.4) (261.5)"); (Q3-10Q page:25 "Purchases (378.2) (132.2) (788.7) (313.8)") | Affiliate dependence for logistics and credits creates related-party leakage and continuity risk outside the issuer's control. |

| Hedging | Commodity derivatives used as economic hedges, not designated as hedges | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:32 "The Company uses derivative instruments to mitigate certain exposures to commodity price risk") | Hedging reduces some price volatility but exposes earnings to mark-to-market swings. |

| Labour | 3,592 employees, 1,899 under collective agreements; several agreements expired or were due to expire in early 2026; outcome not stated | Documentary Fact / Insufficient Information | (10K page:31 "we had approximately 3,592 employees, of which 1,899 are covered by collective bargaining agreements"); (10K page:31 "These collective bargaining agreements have expired or will shortly expire") | Unresolved labour terms are an operating-continuity risk; the pack does not state the outcome. |
### Company profile
| Attribute | Value | Category | Evidence |

| Legal entity | PBF Holding Company LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and holding company for operating subsidiaries; co-registrant PBF Finance Corporation | Documentary Fact | (10K page:11 "We are a Delaware limited liability company and a holding company for our operating subsidiaries") |

| Business description | One of the largest independent petroleum refiners and suppliers of unbranded transportation fuels, heating oil, petrochemical feedstocks, lubricants and other products in the United States | Documentary Fact (self-description) | (10K page:11 "We are one of the largest independent petroleum refiners and suppliers of unbranded transportation fuels") |
| Country and sector | United States; Petroleum Refining (sector from the run context, not issuer evidence) | Documentary Fact | (10K page:11 "in the United States") |
| Segment | One reportable segment of six refineries | Documentary Fact | (10K page:11 "six oil refineries represent one reportable segment") |

| Refineries | Delaware City 180,000 bpd; Paulsboro 155,000 bpd (180,000 at full capacity); Toledo 180,000; Chalmette 185,000; Torrance 166,000; Martinez 157,000 | Documentary Fact | (10K page:12 "Delaware City East Coast 13.6 180,000 1 light sweet through heavy sour water, rail") |

| Direct owner | PBF Energy Company LLC owns 100% of the membership interests | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:2 "100% of the membership interests of PBF Holding Company LLC were owned by PBF Energy Company LLC") |

| Ultimate parent | PBF Energy Inc., sole managing member of PBF LLC with approximately 99.3% of economic interests | Documentary Fact | (10K page:12 "approximately 99.3% of the outstanding economic interests in PBF LLC") |

| Sponsor | None named; listed parent. Not an inference about willingness | Documentary Fact / Insufficient Information | (10K page:12 "On December 18, 2012, our indirect parent, PBF Energy completed its IPO") |

| Affiliates outside the issuer | PBFX (logistics) and SBR (renewable diesel, joint venture with an Eni subsidiary); the issuer has no interest in SBR | Documentary Fact | (10K page:14 "We have no interest in SBR.") |
| Employees | Approximately 3,592 at 2025-12-31 | Documentary Fact | (10K page:31 "we had approximately 3,592 employees") |
| Headquarters | Parsippany, New Jersey | Documentary Fact | (10K page:1 "One Sylvan Way, Second Floor") |
| Reporting basis | Annual report audited; interim reports unaudited; USD millions | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:7 "(unaudited, in millions)") |

| Credit ratings | Notes rated B1 by Moody's, BB by S&P and BB by Fitch at the 10-K date, before the 2026 refinancing; current ratings not supplied | Documentary Fact / Insufficient Information | (10K page:77 "BB by S&P, and BB by Fitch") |

| Guarantors | Eleven wholly owned subsidiaries guarantee the 2034, 2032 exchangeable and 2030 9.875% notes; twelve consolidated subsidiaries are non-guarantors | Documentary Fact | (Q3-10Q page:69 "guarantee the obligations under the 2034 7.25% Senior Notes, the 2032 Exchangeable Notes and the 2030 9.875% Senior Notes") |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues
All items below are Documentary Facts from the issuer's filings unless marked, with their status. No transaction is a sponsor transaction: the context names no sponsor and the pack describes none.

2034 7.25% senior notes. Type: new senior unsecured notes. Parties: PBF Holding and PBF Finance as issuers with certain subsidiary guarantors, Wilmington Trust as trustee. Status: completed 2026-05-28 (Q3-10Q page:21 "the Issuers issued $500.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 2034 7.25% Senior Notes"). Use of proceeds: net proceeds of 492.1 plus available cash redeemed all of the 2028 6.00% notes on 2026-06-25 (Q3-10Q page:23 "On June 25, 2026, the Company redeemed all $801.6 million aggregate principal amount outstanding of its 2028 6.00% Senior Notes"). Terms: guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis, effectively subordinated to secured debt including the revolver, structurally subordinated to non-guarantor subsidiaries, with a change-of-control repurchase at 101% on a ratings decline (Q3-10Q page:23 "at a purchase price of 101% of the principal amount"). Liquidity effect: cash used was the shortfall between the notes redeemed and net proceeds, and the 2028 maturity was removed. Creditor implication: the nearest maturity moved from 2028 to 2034 for this tranche, at a higher coupon than the notes replaced but with maturity extension; Analyst Interpretation.

2032 0.00% exchangeable senior notes. Type: new senior unsecured exchangeable notes with an embedded exchange option and capped call. Parties: PBF Holding and PBF Finance as issuers, PBF Energy Inc. as a party to the indenture and registration rights agreement, U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee. Status: completed 2026-09-17. Amount: 550.0; net proceeds about 533.2, of which 27.7 paid for the capped call and the rest, with cash, redeemed the 2030 7.875% notes (Q3-10Q page:18 "The Issuers used $27.7 million of the net proceeds to pay the cost of the capped call transactions"). Terms: no regular interest and no principal accretion (Q3-10Q page:18 "The 2032 Exchangeable Notes do not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the 2032 Exchangeable Notes will not accrete."), maturity 2032-01-15, initial exchange rate of 10.3306 PBF Energy Class A shares per 1,000 of principal (Q3-10Q page:18 "initial exchange rate is 10.3306 shares of PBF Energy Class A common stock, per $1,000 principal amount"), exchange price about $96.80, capped call cap price about $123.20 (Q3-10Q page:21 "initial cap price of approximately $123.20 per share"), settlement in cash up to principal with the excess in cash or PBF Energy shares at the issuers' election (Q3-10Q page:18 "will be settled in cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being exchanged"). Mechanics: the exchange feature is a bifurcated derivative liability that the issuer marks to fair value, at 197.6 at 2026-09-30 with a 29.9 unrealized loss in Q3 2026, using a PBF Energy share price input of $76.96 (Q3-10Q page:31 "Share price $ 76.96"); the debt host carries a large discount with an effective rate of about 7.0%. Creditor implication: zero cash coupon lowers cash interest, but the issuer carries the principal in cash settlement, the derivative creates earnings volatility linked to the parent's share price, and the instrument depends on parent equity; Analyst Interpretation. A registration rights agreement requires PBF Energy to file a shelf by 2026-12-31 with special interest of 0.25% rising to 0.50% if the issuers fail to comply (Q3-10Q page:20 "on or prior to December 31, 2026").

Redemptions. 2030 7.875% notes: 500.0 redeemed 2026-09-24 at 103.938%, about 519.7 (Q3-10Q page:21 "redeemed at a price equal to 103.938% of the aggregate principal amount thereof"). 2028 6.00% notes: 801.6 redeemed 2026-06-25 at 100%. 2030 9.875% notes: 800.0 redeemed 2026-10-26 at 106.67%, about 853.4, from cash on hand; this is a Subsequent event, with a loss on extinguishment of 70.4 to be booked in Q4 2026 (Q3-10Q page:33 "will be recorded as a Loss on extinguishment of debt in the Consolidated Statements of Operations in the fourth quarter of 2026"). Liquidity effect: cash on hand funds the redemption, reducing cash by about 853.4 plus accrued interest from the 2,510.6 at 2026-09-30. Each redemption was a full redemption of the series, so no holder was treated differently within a series (Analyst Interpretation); no priming, uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange is documented.

Asset-based revolving credit facility. Type: amendment and restatement of the 2023 agreement with Bank of America as administrative agent. Status: effective 2026-09-30 (Q3-10Q page:24 "extended the Revolving Credit Facility through September 30, 2031, increased the maximum commitment from $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion, and reduced the commitment fees on the unused portion"). It was drawn 100.0 at 2025-12-31 and 750.0 at 2026-03-31, and undrawn at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 (financial base handoff). Security: the 10-K describes liens on the parent's equity in the issuer and on receivables, inventory and deposit accounts (10K page:181 "secured by a lien on (i) PBF LLC"), which ranks the revolver ahead of the unsecured notes to the extent of collateral. Executed agreement not supplied.

Hydrogen plants asset purchase. Type: purchase of two hydrogen plants at the Torrance refinery previously under operating leases. Parties: PBF LLC and Air Products; contributed to the issuer. Status: closed 2026-09-09. Issuer accounting: property of about 388.4 recognised, lease liability of 139.7 and right-of-use asset of 140.2 derecognised (Q3-10Q page:13 "PBF LLC contributed the hydrogen production plants to the Company"). The Q2 10-Q described the agreement differently: the issuer "will become the owner and operator", with "a secured promissory note to be issued by PBF LLC" valued at an estimated 320.0 to 340.0 (Q2-10Q page:26 "The transaction includes a secured promissory note to be issued by PBF LLC that will become effective upon closing"). The Q3 10-Q does not mention the note, the security for it or any issuer guarantee. Status of consideration and any lien on the plants: Insufficient Information. This is logged as a conflict below. Creditor implication: operating lease obligations fell, but a secured parent-level note linked to assets now in the issuer's group could affect collateral and restricted-payment capacity if the security touches issuer assets; the pack cannot confirm either way.

Distributions and the parent dividend. Type: recurring distributions to the parent chain. The issuer states it may need to distribute cash to PBF LLC for the parent's dividend of $0.325 per share declared 2026-10-29 and payable 2026-11-24 (Q3-10Q page:33 "The Company may need to make cash distributions to PBF LLC to the extent necessary for PBF Energy to pay this dividend."). Subsequent event; the amount to be distributed by the issuer is not stated.

Martinez refinery fire and insurance. Status: the refinery returned to full operations in May 2026; cumulative insurance proceeds of 1.25 billion net of deductibles (Q3-10Q page:15 "has received cumulative insurance proceeds, net of deductibles and retentions, of $1.25 billion"); investigations by regulators continue and potential liabilities are unknown. Management expects to finalize the insurance claim process before year-end 2026 (Q3-PR page:2 "Working with our insurance group, PBF expects to finalize the claim process before year-end 2026."), a Management Language claim at the parent perimeter.

Chalmette refinery fire. A fire on 2026-05-08 is named among risk factors (Q3-10Q page:5 "the fire on May 8, 2026 at our Chalmette refinery"); no amount, repair timeline or insurance position was found in any pinned source after searching "May 8" and "Chalmette" with fire, outage and incident. Insufficient Information.
### Ownership, control and behaviour
| Item | Documented action or term | Category | Behaviour reading and legal capacity link | Evidence quality |

Risk mechanic: no price floor and no contractual margin, so cash flow tracks external spreads and refinery uptime. Credit implication: debt service capacity is high when spreads are wide and thin when they narrow, as FY2025 showed with Adjusted EBITDA of 29.5; the trailing LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,505.2 rests on two quarters. Counter-evidence logged: management says refining fundamentals remained exceptionally strong (Q3-PR page:1 "refining fundamentals remained exceptionally strong"), Management Language not adopted as a forecast. 2. Refinancing and liquidity. Evidence: the 2026 notes sequence, the revolver extension to 2031-09-30 and cash of 2,510.6 at 2026-09-30 with 800.0 redeemed afterwards. Risk mechanic: removal of 2028 and 2030 maturities and the zero-coupon exchangeable lowers refinancing and interest burden; the secured revolver ranks ahead of unsecured notes in collateral. Credit implication: refinancing risk is low in the near term for this perimeter; effective subordination of the unsecured notes to the revolver and to the parent-linked exchange feature should be monitored. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

3. Concentration. Evidence: Shell at about 13% of revenue, six refineries across four regions. Risk mechanic: customer concentration is modest; asset concentration is in the Martinez and Torrance West Coast refineries and regulatory exposure in California. Credit implication: event risk at one refinery (as the Martinez fire showed) matters more than customer loss. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

4. Sponsor alignment and leakage. Evidence: distributions to the parent chain, asset distributions to PBFX and SBR, parent dividend funding language, hydrogen contribution. 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: unquantified Martinez investigations, the Chalmette fire, the hydrogen note, labour agreements and the missing documents. Credit implication: open items could add cash costs or lien constraints; they are information gaps, not adverse conclusions.

PBF Holding Co LLC (issuer id pbf-holding-co-llc, filed as PBF Holding Company LLC) is assessed as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway, with an evidence cutoff of 2026-11-05. The scope is a fundamental credit synthesis of the issuer perimeter, PBF Holding Company LLC and its consolidated subsidiaries, built only from the accepted financial base and the business and transaction handoffs, in USD millions. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The issuer is financially strong today, with net cash and long-dated maturities, but earnings are cyclical and arrived mostly in two quarters. Open fire, legal and parent-linked items keep the view cautious. | Medium | No forecast or normal-margin earnings view exists, and the financing documents and several event outcomes are missing. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| At 30 September 2026 the issuer held USD 2,510.6 million of cash against USD 1,850.0 million of debt principal, a net cash position of USD 660.6 million. | Near-term default and refinancing risk is low on the reported balance sheet. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA was USD 29.5 million in FY2025 and USD 3,505.2 million for the twelve months to Q3 2026, almost all earned in two quarters. | Leverage and cover ratios depend on whether strong refining margins persist. | Medium |

| After the October 2026 redemption, no drawn debt matures before 2032, and the revolver runs to 2031. | Maturity pressure is minimal, though the exchangeable notes tie the issuer to its parent's share price. | High |

| Cash can move to the parent chain, and fire investigations, a Chalmette fire and the hydrogen plants note remain unquantified or unclear. | These items could consume cash or limit collateral, but their size is not known. | Low |
### Credit view

PBF Holding Company LLC has a sound credit profile at 30 September 2026 that has not yet been tested through a normal-margin year. Its strongest support is liquidity and leverage: USD 2,510.6 million of cash against USD 1,850.0 million of debt principal, net cash of USD 660.6 million, and a USD 4,000.0 million revolver running to 30 September 2031. Its weakest point is earnings durability: Adjusted EBITDA was USD 29.5 million in FY2025 and USD 3,505.2 million over the twelve months to Q3 2026, with USD 3,278.6 million earned in two quarters. What decides the outcome is whether refining margins hold while cash can leave for the parent and the open fire, legal and hydrogen plants items are resolved.
### Key findings

First, the issuer's balance sheet is strong at the latest reported date. Principal debt was USD 1,850.0 million against cash of USD 2,510.6 million, giving net cash of USD 660.6 million and leverage of 0.5x total debt and -0.2x net debt on twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,505.2 million [CP-1 net debt and leverage calculation]. After the redemption of USD 800.0 million of 9.875% notes on 26 October 2026 for about USD 853.4 million, principal falls to USD 1,050.0 million and cash to roughly USD 1,657.2 million before accrued interest and other flows, which is an illustration and not a reported balance [CP-1 illustrative effects]. Category: Documentary Fact for the reported figures, Analyst Interpretation for the illustration.

Second, the issuer's earnings swung from a trough to very high levels, and the trailing figure is concentrated. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 29.5 million in FY2025, USD 1,139.3 million in Q2 2026 and USD 2,139.3 million in Q3 2026 [CP-1 financials table]. The business is priced at spot market and has no contractual margin protection, so the issuer's debt capacity follows crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput and compliance costs [CP-1A operating model]. Management attributes the 2026 strength to conflict-driven market conditions and describes them as uncertain in duration; that is Management Language and is not adopted as a forecast. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Third, the issuer's refinancing in 2026 removed near-term maturities and lowered stated coupon cost. The 6.00% notes due 2028 and 7.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed, USD 500.0 million of 7.25% notes due 2034 and USD 550.0 million of zero-coupon exchangeable notes due 2032 were issued, and the secured revolver was extended with a USD 4,000.0 million commitment [CP-1A transaction summary]. Stated coupons retired of about USD 166.5 million a year compare with about USD 36.3 million on the new fixed notes, excluding revolver fees and discount amortisation. The exchangeable notes settle principal in cash and are linked to the parent's share price, creating a fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million that moves earnings [CP-1 debt instruments; CP-1A transaction summary]. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

Fourth, claims outside the reported debt are material. They include operating lease liabilities of USD 712.3 million at 30 September 2026, pension and post-retirement medical deficits of USD 89.8 million and USD 16.4 million at 31 December 2025, fixed purchase commitments of USD 642.9 million, renewable energy credit and emissions obligations of USD 486.5 million and environmental liabilities of USD 148.4 million, plus unquantified investigations into the Martinez fire and catalyst release [CP-1 claims outside the debt figure]. These rank alongside debt in a downside case and are not in the leverage ratios. Category: Documentary Fact.

Fifth, the issuer's cash flows with its parent were supportive in the downturn and have turned outward as earnings recovered. Parent contributions exceeded distributions by USD 199.6 million in FY2025, but in Q3 2026 distributions exceeded contributions by USD 60.9 million, and the issuer may distribute cash to fund the parent's dividend [CP-1A ownership and behaviour]. Documented behaviour toward creditors is Neutral or Mixed: full redemptions at par or a premium and transparent reporting are supportive, while past asset distributions to affiliates and the parent-level secured note on the hydrogen plants are open. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Sixth, the evidence has gaps that limit how far the view can be pushed: no forecast or through-the-cycle earnings case, no executed indentures or credit agreement, a liquidity figure that cannot be rebuilt, and an unexplained difference between issuer and parent debt figures.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The issuer has low reported leverage and net cash: 0.5x total debt and -0.2x net debt to twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, and cash interest paid of USD 162.3 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,505.2 million, or 21.6x cover on a measure that excludes capitalised interest [CP-1 interest cover]. Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading. The issuer has liquidity depth, with USD 2,510.6 million of cash and about USD 3,100.0 million of rounded borrowing availability, and no revolver drawing at the quarter end [CP-1 liquidity]. Its maturity profile has no drawn debt maturing before 2032 after the October redemption [CP-1 debt maturities]. Its asset base is diversified across six refineries in four regions with one customer at about 13% of revenue, so customer loss is a smaller risk than a single refinery event [CP-1A operating model]. The parent supported the issuer with net contributions of USD 199.6 million in the FY2025 downturn and contributed the hydrogen plants in Q3 2026 [CP-1A ownership and behaviour].

Weaknesses. The issuer's earnings depend on external margins and uptime: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 29.5 million in FY2025 against USD 3,505.2 million over the latest twelve months, with USD 3,278.6 million from two quarters. Analyst Interpretation resting on the CP-1 figures. The issuer faces event risk at single sites: the Martinez fire investigations and the 8 May 2026 Chalmette fire have no quantified impact [CP-1A transaction summary]. Cash can leave to the parent chain and the exchangeable notes link the issuer to the parent's share price, with a fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million [CP-1A behaviour table; CP-1 debt instruments]. Large claims sit outside debt, notably leases, purchase commitments, emissions credits and environmental liabilities [CP-1 claims outside debt]. The revolver is secured and ranks ahead of the unsecured notes to the extent of its collateral; the unsecured notes are also structurally behind non-guarantor subsidiaries, a structural mechanic and not a recovery conclusion [CP-1 debt instruments]. Regulatory compliance cost is large and volatile: renewable fuel compliance cost was USD 522.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 169.0 million a year earlier [CP-1A operating model].
### Assessment and thesis
| Element | Statement | Category | Confidence |

| Fundamental credit view | Sound and well-capitalised at 30 September 2026 on liquidity and leverage, with business risk that is cyclical and event-exposed; the view rests on a short run of strong earnings and is not a through-the-cycle conclusion | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |

| Thesis | PBF Holding Company LLC has used a very strong 2026 margin environment to reach net cash and long-dated maturities, but its credit quality depends on refining margins, refinery uptime and the parent's treatment of cash staying favourable | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |
Confidence is below High because the upstream business handoff records no formal readiness judgment of this module and because the gaps below limit the basis; each gap states what it changes.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Margin reversion | Spot-priced revenue with no margin protection; twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA built on two quarters | Cash generation could fall toward FY2025 levels, leaving fixed charges, capital outlay and distributions to be funded from cash and the revolver | Material |

| Single-site outage or liability | Six refineries, with Martinez and Torrance on the West Coast; unquantified Martinez investigations and a Chalmette fire | An outage cuts throughput and cash flow; penalties and repair costs may exceed insurance, amounts unknown | Material |

| Cash leakage to the parent chain | Distributions to fund parent dividends when liquidity is strong; restricted payment terms not supplied | Liquidity could be reduced faster than earnings are proven durable | Material |

| Parent-linked exchangeable notes | Exchange feature settles on the parent's shares; fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million; principal settled in cash | Earnings volatility from the fair-value liability, and possible cash settlement of value above principal at the issuers' election if the parent's share price rises | Minor |

| Claims outside debt | Leases, pensions, purchase commitments, emissions credits and environmental liabilities | These claims compete with debt service in a downturn and are excluded from leverage | Material |
| Regulatory compliance cost | Renewable fuel credit costs rose to USD 522.8 million in Q3 2026 from USD 169.0 million | Margin compression if credit prices keep rising | Material |

| Hydrogen plants note and security | The parent issued a secured note for plants contributed to the issuer; terms and lien position not described | Possible encumbrance of issuer assets; unknown | Minor |

| Inventory and working capital | Last-in first-out inventory with large price-driven swings in receivables and accruals | A price fall could release working capital but trigger inventory write-downs | Minor |
## Calculations
All inputs are figures already stated in the accepted handoffs; only the arithmetic below is new.
| Item | Formula with inputs | Result |
| Share of twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA earned in Q2 and Q3 2026 | USD 3,278.6 million / USD 3,505.2 million | 93.5% |
| Pro forma total debt to twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA after the October 2026 redemption (illustrative) | USD 1,050.0 million / USD 3,505.2 million | 0.3x |
| Pro forma cash after the redemption price, before accrued interest and other flows (from the financial base handoff) | USD 2,510.6 million - USD 853.4 million | USD 1,657.2 million |
| Pro forma net debt (from the financial base handoff) | USD 1,050.0 million - USD 1,657.2 million | USD -607.2 million (net cash) |
| Cash coverage of a repeat of FY2025 operating cash flow less capital outlay (illustrative) | USD 1,657.2 million / USD 1,418.3 million | 1.2x |

The last line compares illustrative cash after the redemption with the FY2025 figure of operating cash flow less capital outlay of USD -1,418.3 million, which was reported before insurance proceeds classified in investing activities. It is a stress-style illustration of cash cushion in a year like FY2025, not a forecast, and it excludes revolver availability and accrued interest.
## Gaps
| ID | What is missing | Why it matters and what it changes | Severity | Action |
